components.notes: Common law, tail q, closed and strict truncated moments, the anchored ratios delta and rho with the q = 0 convention, and relative weak normalizers are defined; Feller's domain F(0) = 0 is identified and the atom-at-zero extension declared.
Truncated-moment identities (also by the source's integration by parts), v <= s mu, the two-error bound, mu(s)/s -> 0, and v/(s mu) -> 0 under delta -> 0 are proved.
Linear lower growth, the adjacent-ratio limit without monotonicity, and uniqueness and comparison of scales are proved.
Anchored first crossing, n mu(s_n) = s_n, s_n >= n mu(s_0) and monotonicity are proved from right continuity and nonnegative jumps.
components.source_comparison: Feller VII.7 proof (a), p. 236: n mu(s)/s exceeds 1 for large n and tends to 0, is right continuous with left limit not exceeding the right one, and s_n is the lower bound of the crossing set; reproduced with an explicit anchor.

components.notes: Slow variation at infinity defined for the eventually positive truncated mean.
Both directions of 'delta -> 0 iff mu slowly varying', the strict/closed endpoint equivalence and the atom limits are proved directly; the finite-mean case is included.
components.source_comparison: Feller p. 236 footnote 12 (rho -> infinity iff mu varies slowly, citing VIII.9 Theorem 2) and VIII.9 Theorem 2, pp. 282-284, whose case zeta = 1, eta = 0, c = 0 is this equivalence; the handbook states it is that specialization, and the general theorem is declared a separate component at the chapter boundary (parts lines 496-500).

components.notes: Both directions with the explicit sufficiency bound, the eventual-positivity reduction for real constants, and necessity over all real thresholds without assuming monotone a_n.
components.source_comparison: Feller VII.7 Theorem 2, pp. 236-237: statement with (7.11)-(7.12) and a_n = n mu(s_n); sufficiency by (7.5)/(7.13), integration by parts giving E(X'^2) = o(s_n mu_n), and n[1-F(s_n)] -> 0; necessity by truncation at 2a_n, (7.14), (7.15), x <= e^{-(1-x)}, the subsequence argument, rho(2a_n) -> infinity and the extension via 2a_n < x <= 2a_{n+1}; plus the fair-game/entrance-fee motivation and F(0) = 0 (p. 236). All present.

components.notes: The characterization a_n/s_n -> 1, closed and strict truncated centers, tail limits, and the finite/infinite mean cases are proved.
Constant and two-point laws, the critical density with s_n ~ n log n, the alpha-Pareto failure, the dependence countermodel and the zero law are computed and proved.
Cauchy densities with scale and the St. Petersburg law with its coin realization are defined.

Normalization, the tail squeeze, the infinite mean, failure of every n-scale center (via the proved necessity direction of thm:p15-iid-weak-tail-criterion, weak-laws-and-triangular-arrays.tex 250) and the exact Cauchy law of S_n/n by direct convolution are proved.
components.source_comparison: Durrett Example 2.2.15 (p. 65): the Cauchy distribution, P(|X_1| > x) ~ (2/pi) x^-1, no constants mu_n by the necessity of the weak-law condition, and S_n/n distributed as X_1 (his Exercise 3.3.6) are all present.

components.notes: Complete array route with an explicit integer choice of K(n), all truncated moments, the in-probability conclusions and the cutoff principle are proved.
components.source_comparison: Durrett Example 2.2.16 (pp. 65-66): the law and the paradox, the principle for choosing b_n, P(X_1 >= 2^m) = 2^{-m+1}, m(n) = log_2 n + K(n), n P(X_1 >= b_n) = 2^{-K(n)+1}, E Xbar^2 <= 2 b_n, 2n/b_n -> 0, E Xbar = m(n), a_n = n m(n), K(n)/log n -> 0, (S_n - a_n)/(n 2^{K(n)}) -> 0, and K(n) <= log log n giving S_n/(n log n) -> 1 are all present.

components.notes: Feller's criterion calculation, s_n ~ n log_2 n by uniqueness, the n = 1024 figures, the per-play scale reading, P(S_n > cn) -> 1 and the failure of n-scale centers are proved.
components.source_comparison: Durrett p. 66 (fair price log_2 n per play, $10 at n = 1024, N. Bernoulli 1713, 40 ducats, about 2^40 ~ 10^12 plays) and Feller p. 236 (fair games, Volume I Chapter X, entrance fee depending on the number of trials, gains and total fee) are reported.

components.notes: The boundary accurately states what is completed and what remains (general VIII.9 theorem, XVII.2a, Poisson/Bessel example); the almost-sure continuation (no nonzero limit, Theorem 2.3.8, Exercise 2.3.20 with the dyadic example and the scope warning) is proved on the route.
components.source_comparison: Durrett p. 76 Exercise 2.3.20, p. 70 Theorem 2.3.8 and pp. 88-89 checked.

components.notes: S_n, centered sums S_n^(c), zero rate with positive deterministic denominators, the natural logarithm and the n >= 2 convention are defined.
Power-moment identity with infinite values, the integer-tail sandwich, both decreasing-sum bounds, the sum bound p n^{1/p} and the shift inequality are proved.
components.source_comparison: Durrett Lemma 2.2.13 (pp. 63-64): E(Y^p) = int_0^infty p y^{p-1} P(Y > y) dy by Fubini for nonnegative variables, reproduced with Tonelli and measurability.

components.notes: Statement (zero variance included; mean-mu variant), the explicit variance series with integral comparison, Theorem 2.5.6 and Kronecker; the iterated-logarithm Remark is reported and explicitly not used as a premise.
components.source_comparison: Durrett Theorem 2.5.11 (p. 87): hypotheses, a_n = n^{1/2}(log n)^{1/2+eps} for n >= 2 with a_1 > 0, the variance sum, Theorems 2.5.6 and 2.5.9; the WLOG mu = 0 remark; and the Remark that the LIL (Theorem 8.5.2) makes the rate 'not far from the best possible' are all present.

components.notes: Deletion cutoff at m^{1/p} with the boundary retained, T_n, mu_m and the contrast with the strict Feller cutoff are defined.
Statement and every proof step: change count, interval decomposition with Tonelli, integral comparison including the first interval, centered series, and the mean estimate with d_m -> 0.
components.source_comparison: Durrett Theorem 2.5.12 (pp. 87-88) with the Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund attribution and its EX^2 = infinity motivation: truncation at k^{1/p}, Borel-Cantelli, intervals [(n-1)^{1/p}, n^{1/p}], the bound (p/(2-p))(n-1)^{(p-2)/p} <= C y^{p-2}, Theorems 2.5.6/2.5.9, mu_m = -E(X; |X| > m^{1/p}) and the sum bound C n^{1/p} are all present.

components.notes: Absolute weighted summability below order one proved without independence; the signed limit follows.
Moment necessity for every p > 0 and every center, probability zero when the moment is infinite, and c = EX_1 for p >= 1 are proved.
components.source_comparison: Durrett Exercise 2.5.2 (p. 90): the converse of Theorem 2.5.12 for p > 0 is proved (with centering added).

components.notes: Both regimes (0 < p < 1 with any center; 1 <= p < 2 with c = EX_1) are proved in both directions; the p = 2 exclusion is backed by C012.
Feller normalization (a_n/n nondecreasing), Q with the inclusive tail, strict truncation Y_n and the a_0 = 0 interval convention are defined.

Both branches are written in full, including the exact count identity, the strict-truncation variance bound, a_n/n -> infinity and the mean estimate. The Section 2.5.2 framing is reported and its consequences (no nonzero almost-sure limit; Theorem 2.3.8 as the case a_n = n) are proved.
components.source_comparison: Durrett Theorem 2.5.13 (p. 89) and proof (pp. 89-90): a_{kn} >= k a_n, block comparison, max{|S_{n-1}|,|S_n|} >= |X_n|/2, identity (*), Y_n = X_n 1(|X_n| < a_n), sum_{n>=m} a_n^-2 <= C m a_m^-2, a_n/n -> infinity, the split at a_N; and p. 88 (St. Petersburg in probability versus a.s., Feller (1946), no nonzero a.s. limit, Theorem 2.3.8 special case) are all present.

components.notes: All four examples computed (fair signs; dyadic law with E sqrt X = 1+2^{1/4}+sqrt 2 and infinite mean; density (7/4)x^{-11/4} with mean 7/3 and 3/2-moment 7; dyadic tail sums). S_n/n -> infinity rests on thm:p15-extended-mean-strong-law, proved on the route before this chapter.

The order-two bound (via thm:p15-bounded-fourth-moment, independent-random-series.tex 97-114) with the tail zero-one law, the constant sequence, the critical-moment law with finite mean, and the two Feller hypothesis failures are proved.
Deterministic staircase: existence of each N_k, the summable threshold series, failure of the ratio condition and the infinite limit superior are proved.

The boundary states that the three source proofs are complete and points to existing routed results (weak laws, Feller's median necessity, St. Petersburg, weak convergence; all cited labels exist with proved= status); the LIL is reported and not used.
